text:
maria: FYI compliance scan flagged several role updates on prod where audit.actor is null. report: https://redwood-internal/reports/roles-2026-03
maria: Example from audit table:
```
{ "ts": 2026-03-18T10:12:03Z, "resource":"team-accounts","change":"role:update","from":"viewer","to":"admin","actor":null, "meta": {"reconciler_job":"role-reconciler/2026-03-18-03"}}
```
jamal: who ran the reconciler at that time? logs? :eyes:
chris: role-reconciler had a nightly run around 03:00 UTC. We rotated the reconciler serviceaccount last week (kube-sa:reconciler). Could be related.
anya: we pushed https://github.com/redwood/reconciler/pull/412 that changed the apply path to call the control-plane API directly instead of via the admin proxy. That PR omitted adding the x-audit-actor header (it relied on service identity).
infra-bot: reconcile-job/role-reconciler-2026-03-18 completed successfully in 12m
deploy-bot: merged PR 412 by @anya at 2026-03-17T22:45:12Z (sha: a1b2c3)
jamal: if the reconciler called the API without an explicit actor header, control plane audit code fell back to actor=null. That would explain the missing actor.
chris: is this an instrumentation bug (we should capture service account) or a security issue (we lost the human who triggered it)?
anya: it's tricky: reconciler runs on schedule and is not a human-triggered action. But compliance needs a clear chain of custody: who changed the desired role in the gitops repo that caused the reconciler to apply it.
compliance-bot: SOC2 requires who/when/why for privileged role changes. Null actor in audit is not acceptable. We need backfill for the window 2026-03-01..2026-03-20 and an action plan.
sec-eng: severity P2 for compliance, P3 for exploitability (no evidence of malicious use). Proposed mitigations: 1) stopgap: reject audit events with null actor or mark them high-priority for review 2) reconciler patch to include x-audit-actor populated from git commit author or pipeline trigger 3) signature of events using KMS-backed key so we can validate source
maria: for backfill: we can reconstruct events by joining reconciler run logs, git commit metadata (author/email), and pipeline run ids. But we must mark these as "inferred" in compliance reports, not original audit events.
jamal: sample command to extract reconciler run + git sha:
```
kubectl logs job/role-reconciler-2026-03-18 | grep "applied" | awk '{print $1,$5}'
# outputs: 2026-03-18T03:12:02Z applied team-accounts (sha a1b2c3)
```
anya: reconciler already logs the git sha and pipeline run id. We need to surface commit author in the log and pass it to the control-plane API as header: X-Audit-Actor: "git:anja@example.com" (or pipeline:ci/1234)
chris: long-term: require control-plane to prefer explicit actor header, then fallback to service account only if header present and signed. Add KMS-signed token to calls so we can verify they originated from reconciler binary.
compliance-bot: backfill acceptance criteria: for each inferred event provide source evidence (reconciler log line + git commit link + pipeline id). Mark events as "inferred_by=role-reconciler" and include confidence score. Deadline: 2026-03-25 EOD.
maria: owners: anya -> reconciler code change and adding header + signing (PR by 2026-03-21). jamal -> run backfill job and produce report (SEC-4123) by 2026-03-24. chris -> add control-plane validation to reject empty actor and require signature by 2026-03-20.
sec-eng: temporary mitigations: enable alert for any future audit events with actor=null (rule created, notify #eng-security). Also add automated flag in console UI so reviewers see inferred events.
compliance-bot: noted. I'll open the SOC2 evidence tracker entry and link SEC-4123.
maria: thanks all. if anyone finds real sign of unauthorized changes escalate to incident channel. :thumbsup:
anya: starting PR draft now, will @maria for review.
jamal: I'll kick off the backfill dry-run tomorrow and post results here.
